seeds.scene: A moving van's interior with dimensions printed on the side: 240 cm wide × 180 cm high × 360 cm deep. A king-size mattress to be loaded measures 198 cm × 203 cm × 30 cm thick. The van's rear door opening is 200 cm wide × 175 cm high.
seeds.question: Can the mattress fit through the door (in any orientation)?
seeds.lever: Door is 200×175; mattress in flat orientation needs 30×203 → 30 fits in 175, 203 > 200 → won't fit flat through door horizontally. But sliding diagonally with 30cm thickness: 30×175 = leaves 198×30 cross-section → 198 fits in 200 width? Yes. Push mattress diagonally tilted through 200 wide door, since 30 thick fits height-wise. Verify: standing mattress on edge (203 vertical) — door height only 175, so 203 won't fit upright. Tilt 30°: mattress projection at angle... Check: at angle θ, projected diagonal = 203·cosθ + 30·sinθ ≤ 175 (height) and 198·cosθ + 30·sinθ ≤ 200 (width). At θ=30°, 203·0.866+30·0.5=175.8+15=190.8 > 175. Need θ larger. At θ=45°: 203·0.707+30·0.707=164.7 ≤ 175 ✓; width 198·0.707+30·0.707=161 ≤ 200 ✓. So yes, fits diagonally.
